t.3.61.1: Rāma, thus tormented and worn down by the abduction of Sītā, intent upon the destruction of the worlds like the Saṃvartaka fire at the dissolution of the universe…
t.3.61.2: Him, gazing at his strung bow and sighing again and again, like Rudra enraged at Dakṣa's sacrifice, eager to slay the sacrificial beast.
t.3.61.3: Seeing Rāma enraged as never before, Lakṣmaṇa, with joined palms and a face gone dry, spoke these words.
t.3.61.4: Having formerly been gentle, self-controlled, and devoted to the welfare of all beings, you ought not, now fallen under the sway of anger, to abandon your true nature.
t.3.61.5: In the moon there is beauty, in the sun radiance, in the wind motion, and on the earth forbearance; all this is fixed and constant, and in you there is unsurpassed glory.
t.3.61.6: But I do not know whose war-chariot this is that lies broken here, together with its weapons and its equipment, nor by whom it was broken, or for what reason.
t.3.61.7: And this ground, O son of a king, torn up by hooves and wheel-rims and sprinkled with drops of blood, is a most dreadful place where a battle has been fought.
t.3.61.8: This trampling is the work of one alone, not of two, O best of speakers; for I see no trace here of a great army having been.
t.3.61.9: But you ought not to destroy the worlds for the sake of a single person. For lords of the earth are gentle and tranquil, inflicting punishment only as is fitting.
t.3.61.10: You have always been the refuge of all beings, their supreme resort; who, O Rāghava, could possibly regard the loss of your wife as a good thing?
t.3.61.11: Rivers, oceans, mountains, gods, gandharvas and dānavas are not able to do you any harm, just as the virtuous cannot wrong one who is consecrated for a sacrifice.
t.3.61.12: O king, you ought to search for the one by whom Sītā was carried off, with me as your companion, bow in hand, and with the supreme seers as your helpers.
t.3.61.13: We shall search the ocean, the mountains and the forests, the many kinds of dreadful caves, and the lotus ponds of the mountains as well.
t.3.61.14: With focused minds we shall search the worlds of the devas and the gandharvas as well, until we find the one who carried off your wife.
t.3.61.15: If the lords of the thirty gods do not give back your wife through conciliation, O lord of Kosala, then afterwards you shall do what the moment demands.
t.3.61.16: If, O lord of men, you will not regain Sītā through good conduct, conciliation and humility, the very means by which she is not being won, then lay everything waste with floods of golden-feathered arrows like the thunderbolt of great Indra.
